function: Externalises the fifth and last of the five 88-level lookup tables declared
in the frozen COBOL copybook app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy as classpath reference
data. The table is the set of four-character combinations of a
two-character state code followed by the first two digits of a zip code,
accepted when validating the state-and-zip portion of a customer address.

sourceCopybookRole: The COBOL corpus under app/ is frozen and read-only. It is simultaneously
the parity oracle, the field-contract source and the traceability anchor
for this migration, so it is never edited, moved or reformatted.
parentDataItemNote: The single condition name below is an 88-level on this four-character
subfield, so every value is exactly four characters of PIC X data: two
letters of state code followed by the first two digits of a zip code.
The 88-level is declared on this subfield alone and on nothing else,
which is what fixes the element width at four and makes the enclosing
group item and the sibling subfield recorded below explanatory rather
transcription: Every value is transcribed verbatim from the frozen COBOL corpus, in source
order, with no value added, removed, sorted, deduplicated, re-cased or
reformatted. A value that differs from the copybook is a parity break, not
a correction: the copybook is the sole authority.
extractionMethod: Comment-skipping literal extraction: within the inclusive line range, a
line whose first non-blank character is '*' is a COBOL comment and is
skipped; every remaining single-quoted literal is collected in source
order. Two properties of this table make fixed-column slicing unsafe, so
it is not used. First, the continuation lines are indented with spaces
alone and contain no horizontal tab at all, an indentation unique to this
table among the five - the three area-code tables use two tabs with no
leading space and the state-code table uses one space followed by two
tabs - so an extractor written against either of them silently drops
values here. Second, the 88-level clause line carries no value at all,
unlike the area-code tables whose clause line carries the first value;
the first value here is on the following line. Assuming otherwise drops
'AA34' and shifts every index, which is a Blocker. Extraction is verified
against a whole-file total of 1276 literals across all five tables, being
statementTerminator: The final source line reads 'WY83'. - the trailing period closes the COBOL
statement and is not part of the value. Extraction stops at that line: the
sibling subfield declared immediately below it, and the version-stamp
comment lines that follow it, contribute nothing and are not data.
interiorComment: None. No comment line falls inside the value range, so no line is skipped
within it. The comment line immediately above the group item at
app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy:L1070 introduces this table and describes it
accurately, but it is documentation and its text is deliberately not
carried into this resource, neither as data nor as a description. It is
also the line the sibling resource us-state-codes.json cites as the far
networkSources: None. The copybook cites no external registry for this table, so there is
nothing to reference even historically. No postal-service zip database,
no zip-code service and no other external source was consulted. No value
is fetched, refreshed or reconciled over the network at build time or run
time, and this resource performs no outbound access of any kind. A
combination that differs from the copybook is a parity break, not a fix.
groupItemNote: The enclosing group item is seven characters wide and carries no PIC
clause of its own: it is subdivided into the four-character validated
subfield recorded above and the three-character sibling subfield recorded
below, so together they hold a two-character state code and a full
five-digit zip code. Only the first four of those seven characters

observation: This sibling subfield carries no 88-level, in this copybook or
anywhere else in the corpus, so the last three digits of a zip
code are never validated by the legacy system. The source line
pads the name out to its PIC clause with eleven spaces rather
than one: a cosmetic legacy irregularity, severity Low, preserved
uncorrected in the frozen corpus because it has no effect on the
disposition: Nothing is transcribed for it. No last-three-digits array, no
full-zip list and no zip range appears in this resource, because
there is no rule to transcribe. Inventing one would introduce a
validation the legacy system does not perform, which is a
behaviour change rather than a correction, and the data would be

note: This is the frozen copybook's own version stamp, quoted as provenance
evidence. It is NOT a generation timestamp for this resource, which has
none: no value in this file is environment-specific or time-dependent,
so identical inputs always produce identical bytes. The stamp is
deterministic precisely because it is a fixed constant of the frozen

summary: The complete set of state-and-zip-prefix combinations accepted by
the legacy validation. The declaration line and the first value
line differ because the 88-level clause line carries no value,
which is why both ranges are recorded above.
Ordering is source ordering: ascending by the two-character state
prefix, but NOT always ascending in the two-digit zip part within
a prefix, and with many numeric gaps. Indices 150 to 157 are
run in the table where the zip part descends. Sorting it into
The 240 values yield 62 distinct two-character prefixes. That
count is derived, not declared: it is stated here for verification
and is deliberately not duplicated as a separate array, which
could only drift out of step with the data.
The rule the consumer applies is membership in this array on the
first four characters of the input, and nothing else.

invariants: The element count is exactly 240; any other count is a Blocker.
Every element is a JSON string of exactly four characters matching
^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{2}$ - two uppercase ASCII letters then two digits - never a
number, because the source field is PIC X(4) character data and every value
begins with letters.
No element is null, empty, whitespace-padded, lower-cased or duplicated.
Each element is the four-character source string, flat and unmodified. It is
never split into a state-and-zip object or a two-element tuple, never
grouped or indexed by state prefix, never given a separator such as
'AA-34', and never padded towards a five-digit zip. Every one of those
shapes loses the exact source string; grouping by prefix would additionally
destroy source ordering and make the descending NY run unrepresentable.
Contiguous runs are never compacted into ranges such as 'NJ70-NJ89'. The
array holds 240 discrete strings.
The order is source order. Sorting, deduplicating or gap-filling the array
is a Blocker: each one changes which addresses validate. The numeric gaps
are genuine and every one is preserved - no VT55, no TX74, no VI81, no
AE99 and no VA21; MO65 followed by MO72; MA27 followed by MA55; ME
beginning at ME39; DC as 'DC20' 'DC56' 'DC88'; and PR60 to PR79 followed
by PR90 to PR98.
This table appears in exactly one resource. It is never merged with,
derived from, or reconciled against the other two validation resources,
and it is never duplicated as generated Java constants.
Cross-resource property, observed and intentional in the source: the
sibling resource us-state-codes.json holds 56 state codes and all 56 are a
subset of the 62 prefixes here. The 6 extra prefixes are AA, AE and AP,
which are military and diplomatic mail designations, and FM, MH and PW,
which are Freely Associated States; 56 + 6 = 62. Those 6 are valid
zip-prefix combinations but are deliberately NOT accepted state codes.
Removing 'AA34', 'AE90' to 'AE98', 'AP96', 'FM96', 'MH96' or 'PW96' from
this array, or adding those prefixes to the sibling, is a Blocker: it
silently alters which addresses validate.

metadataHandling: This _metadata member is documentation, NOT data. The consuming service
ignores it explicitly and deliberately by its well-known name; it is never
bound as a lookup table and never participates in validation.
bindingContract: Read as UTF-8 from the classpath and bound with plain, explicitly typed
Jackson binding to string collections. No polymorphic type handling and no
default typing are used or required, and this resource carries no type
hint of any kind, so it cannot drive insecure deserialisation.
exposure: Loaded once at startup into immutable collections, so no caller can mutate
shared lookup state. A 240-element set held immutably answers the
membership question in constant time and needs no index or grouping

whatItDoes: Supplies the single table that the legacy 88-level condition name
VALID-US-STATE-ZIP-CD2-COMBO expressed in COBOL. A membership test
against this array replaces evaluating that condition name, and is what
decides whether the state-and-zip-prefix portion of a customer address
is accepted. The input to that test is the first four characters of the
seven-character state-and-zip field: the two-character state code and
the first two digits of the zip code.
howToBuildAndTest: No build step: this is a static classpath resource copied verbatim into
target/classes by the standard resources phase, with no property
filtering. Build with './mvnw -B clean compile' and run the unit suite with
'./mvnw -B clean test'. The assertions for this resource live under
src/test/java/com/cardemo/unit/ and cover the element count of 240, the
first and last values 'AA34' and 'WY83', the interior index checkpoints
60 'KS66', 120 'NH33' and 180 'PR71', the preserved descending NY run at
indices 150 to 157, the absence of the gap values, the 62 distinct
prefixes, and the subset relationship with the sibling state-code
configurationAndDefaults: No configuration and no defaults: the content is fixed reference data and
there is no property, profile or environment variable that alters it.
The resource path itself is the only contract with the consumer.
Encoding is UTF-8 with LF line endings and two-space indentation, per the
commonFailureModesAndTroubleshooting: Resource not found on the classpath: the consumer must fail fast and
loudly rather than degrade to an empty table, because an empty table
would silently reject every customer address. Confirm the file is
present under target/classes/validation/ after a build.
Malformed content: the consumer must wrap the parse failure with this
resource path and preserve the root cause. Re-validate the file with a
strict JSON parser.
Unexpected element count: compare against the count of 240 published in
sourceTables above. A mismatch means the resource was truncated or
edited, and it is a Blocker - re-derive it from app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy.
A valid address rejected that the legacy system accepted: verify the
combination against the copybook line range, never against any external
zip list. The usual causes are an extractor that sliced fixed columns or
split on horizontal tabs - this table alone of the five uses spaces only
- and one that treated the 88-level clause line as carrying the first
value and so lost 'AA34', shifting every index by one.
Ordering reported as wrong because the zip part descends across indices
150 to 157, or because numbers are missing from a run: both are expected
and correct. Do not sort the array and do not fill the gaps.
The last three digits of a zip code appearing unvalidated: that is the
legacy behaviour, because no 88-level is declared on LAST-3-OF-ZIP.
A privacy note for the consumer rather than for this file: a state code
with a zip prefix is a fragment of a customer address, so the value
being looked up must never be written to a log line.

designRationale: This table is data, not code. Generating it as Java constants would put
reference data into a compilation unit, make the count harder to audit and
add source that no compiler check makes safer - and across the five tables
of this copybook it would run to well over a thousand lines. Externalising
it as a classpath resource keeps the membership exactly auditable against
the copybook, keeps the count visible for verification, and is the
The flat four-character string is the maintainable shape as well as the
faithful one: it is the source string itself, so it needs no assembly, no
parsing and no reconciliation, and a 240-element immutable set answers the
membership question in constant time without any further structure.
notAvailable: Any documented rationale in the source for the descending NY run at
indices 150 to 157, or for the numeric gaps within the state prefixes:
Not available. The copybook declares the values and their order and
documents no rule for either, so no behaviour is inferred from them and
both are reproduced rather than tidied. To resolve this, what is needed is
an authoritative statement of the rule from the system owner, or a postal
specification admitted into the repository as a reference artefact.
Any documented rationale in the source for why AA, AE, AP, FM, MH and PW
are valid zip-prefix combinations yet are not accepted state codes:
Not available. The copybook declares both sets and documents no rule, and
no postal or territorial specification exists anywhere in this repository,
so no behaviour is inferred from the difference and the asymmetry is
reproduced rather than reconciled. The same authoritative statement or
reference artefact is what would be needed to resolve it.
Any rule governing the last three digits of a zip code:
Not available, and none exists in the source. LAST-3-OF-ZIP carries no
88-level, so the legacy system performs no such validation and there is
nothing to transcribe. Adding one would need a stated rule from the system
owner, which no artefact in this repository supplies.
A lookup latency or throughput objective:
Not available. The legacy source publishes no service level of any kind,
so none is invented here; the performance gate records a measured baseline
rather than a target. To set one, what is needed is a stated objective
from the system owner, which no artefact in this repository supplies.
